contexts.text: It is then predicated of the Lord... that He lifts up His face upon him.
To lift up the eyes and see = to be illuminated and to perceive.
To lift up the eyes = to see and perceive the things which are above one's self, (that is, the things which are interior.) Explained.
To lift up the voice and weep = the last extremity of grief.
To lift up the eyes = to elevate the intelligence, thus to think. AC 2829. AC 3198.
To lift up the eyes and see = intention.
Jacob lifted up his feet () = the elevation of the Natural. To lift up = elevation.
To lift up the voice and weep = the ardour of love.
Rational and voluntary things from the Divine were then given, which are signified by its being lifted up from the earth ().
To lift up the eyes = to think, and also to intend, thus to perceive. (And thus also to advert. AC 4086.) AC 4339. AC 4988.
For to lift up the eyes is an external thing which corresponds to the elevation of the mind... consequently, to perception. AC 4356.
To lift up the eyes and see = intention and thought, or intense thought; here, further thought.
To lift up the voice and cry = great aversion.
Pharaoh shall lift up thy head () = what is foreseen and thence concluded. Illustrated.

To lift up the head = their deliverance; for they are then elevated or lifted up out of vastation, to the heavenly Societies. To be lifted up or to be elevated = to progress towards interior things... Whereas to lift up the head from upon anyone = to be judged to death. Explained.
Pharaoh shall lift up thy head from upon thee () = what is concluded from what is foreseen. Explained. AC 5162.
Under Hand, see this reference. AC 5328. AC 7211. AR 474.
To lift up the eyes = thought and intention... and also advertence, thus reflection. Explained.
This is why the Lord so greatly extols His own power and glory.
Still to lift himself () = not as yet to desist from infesting.
To lift up the eyes = mental view, perception, and thought. References.
To bear, and take away, evil = to remove it so that it does not appear; for the evils with a man cannot be taken away...
To take away sins means the same as redeeming man, and saving him. Explained.
To take up the cross = to fight against concupiscences.
To take away peace from the earth () = charity etc. taken away.
See Horn.
To lift up (His faces) = to reveal Himself, which is effected from the Divine good through the Divine truth. AE 412:4.
To extol = confession.
To lift up the eyes = to take notice.
To lift up the voice = their joy from Knowledge.
